page: Microsoft Azure L8as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 8 dedicated virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, it operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The VM includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, 32 MB of L3 cache, and 64 GB of system RAM, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. Local storage consists of a direct-attached 2006 GB NVMe SSD, providing dense high-speed scratch space directly on the host.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core CPU execution, with stress-ng single-core reaching 2710.47 points, placing it in the upper quartile. Multi-core compute performance sits firmly in the middle tier, yielding 10802.55 in stress-ng multi-core and 6373.0 in Geekbench multi-core. In memory workloads, cached read bandwidth achieves 515.46 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read (38.93 GB/sec) and write (22.95 GB/sec) metrics reflect lower architectural memory bandwidth ceilings typical of shared-host hypervisor allocations. In application tests, it handles 8.23 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.03 GB/sec in static web throughput.

The balance of 8 vCPUs, 64 GB RAM, and a bundled 2 TB NVMe drive offers high qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads needing local disk caching without auxiliary network storage fees. However, lack of AVX-512 extensions and lower large-block memory throughput restrict efficiency for heavy vectorized compute or large-scale AI modeling. The instance is suited for transactional databases, NoSQL engines, distributed data caching, and log indexing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L8as_v3 is a storage-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, running at 3.525 GHz. It includes 64 GB of memory (8 GB per vCPU) and features a bundled 2006 GB NVMe SSD for fast local data access. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread performance alongside solid mid-tier multi-threaded and database results, achieving 8.23 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.03 GB/sec in static web throughput. Tradeoffs include modest uncached memory bandwidth and the omission of AVX-512 capabilities, making it less suited for large matrix compute workloads. Overall, the combination of substantial memory and integrated high-capacity NVMe makes this instance suitable for I/O-heavy relational and NoSQL databases, log analysis clusters, and local caching layers.
